title: Top-level executable code placed after the first :: directive
purpose: Prevent silently-dead prolog code, which produces a program that compiles cleanly and runs with zero output instead of failing loudly.
trigger: An ooRexx source file contains a top-level (non-directive, non-comment) executable statement appearing after the first ::CLASS/::METHOD/::ROUTINE/::REQUIRES line. Once directive space begins, it does not end -- there is no way back into prolog space later in the same file.
evidence_note: Directly observed this session: a test script was written with ::class TestPokerTable as the first construct in the file, followed by the intended main-flow code (assignments, decide() calls, say statements). The file compiled without error and executed with no output at all -- the prolog was never reached, because directive space had already started at the top of the file. Restructuring to prolog-first, directives-last fixed it immediately.
correct: All top-level executable statements (the program's main flow, including any internal routines it calls via CALL or function-call syntax) must appear before the first :: directive. ::CLASS/::METHOD/::REQUIRES etc. belong at the end of the file, after `exit`.
compiler_relationship: ooRexx does not raise a syntax error for this -- the file is fully valid, just structured so the intended entry point is unreachable. Silent-wrong-behaviour class of bug, not a translator failure.
return_semantics: A LanguageRulePage may be opened and then return to the originating cycle selector.
